docs.title: aka @cooper on Hack Club's Slack
docs.text:
You can call me Jack because I am jack of all trades but master of one.

I work across the following fields:

  • Desktop, Mobile and Web Software Development (Super power: I build fault-tolerant systems)

  • Leadership roles like events organizer or just mentor a team of juniors.

  • Sometimes I teach AI and ethics, and whatever I am completely sure of (I don't pass half info)
  • I spend my time thinking about political policies, geo-political situations and more. Not because I am uncle, but because I have a really good reason to do so.

docs.title: What am I doing now ?
docs.text:
I just finished my high school, so I am free. Currently, I am working on NID-24 a musclar intent classification system that works as a biological human device interface.

This project is for Hack Club's Fallout

I have a few more projects in my GitHub's Graveyard

docs.title: You might think, is this your portfolio ?
docs.text:
The answer is yes. I am quite busy with the fallout project. Plus, I am too lazy to work with a framework which is based on another framework derived from the pyramid of abstractions.

This static website covers everything - My projects, stories and everything. What else do I need ?

docs.title: My Garage
docs.text:
A collection of systems, frameworks, and hardware-software interfaces I have built. I focus on building tools that are fault-tolerant, accessible, and low-level.

Each award winning project was a year long journey which came with lessons that really changed me. I have put those stories in my book so it's worth reading the chapters.

I also have unshipped projects on my GitHub which includes some projects that I made for inter-school competitions. I won them mostly but never got the 1st position. I haven't got my certificates yet.

AVERAGE INDIAN SCHOOL COMEPTITIONS

docs.title: 1. Vulture OS
docs.text:
National Finalist: IIT Bombay Techfest 2022

  • Award: Budding Innovator
  • Concept: Fault-tolerant Home Automation OS
  • Stack: C++, Qt Framework
  • Status: Shipped (Legacy), I didn't know about Github and Git that much.

Vulture OS was a home automation platform/OS which my first piece of fault-tolerant system. I began ideating when my IoT project failed at school exhibition. I was just super furious on Blynk, and still I am because of their new business model.

But this project won 2 awards - Youngest National Finalist & Budding Innovator at IIT Bombay Techfest 2022

PS: This project also failed during final presentation because of a network authentication protocol which I didn't account for it was a commercial network I was trying to connect to and it failed.

docs.title: 2. Project "Key" (IFT Season 3)
docs.text:
National Top 6 Finalist

  • Competition: India's Future Tycoons (IFT) Season 3
  • Visibility: Featured on CNN Mirror Now
  • Status: Shipped (Legacy), I still didn't know about Github and Git that much.

During lock-down I started my journey as a programmer, online classes were difficult for teachers because they were not really used to computers. So, me and my friend made this application which bought all the tools at one place with simple interface making online classes a bit efficient.

PS: This also failed during final presentation due to the way I configured speech recognition module.

docs.title: 3. NID-24 (Next-gen Interface Device)
docs.text:
Status: Under Active Development

  • Concept: EMG-based Human-Device Interface (HDI)
  • Hardware: Muscle sensors + Signal processing
  • Repo: Raghav67816/NID-24

NID-24 is my current research project into gesture-based computing. It utilizes Electromyography (EMG) to capture electrical activity from human muscles, allowing for device control without physical touch or cameras. I am currently working on the PCB design because it is most fundamental part of this project.

docs.title: 4. The Layman's AI Framework
docs.text:
Status: Shipped

  • The Goal: Making Neural Networks transparent for students.
  • Stack: Python, Custom Math/Linear Algebra
  • Repo: Raghav67816/The-Layman-AI-Framework

I love this one, so basically our education board's curriculum for AI is really worse, and we have been studying the same thing in AI for past 4 years and we were using some really useless tools like teachable machines which give you surface level knowledge only. But using intermidiate or advanced tools was not an option either.

So, with the help of my teacher, I studied learning patterns of my batchmates, and made a tensorflow but the simplest version such that it matches the language written in the worst book I have ever read.

PS: This one rocked. I got 50/50 with this project in my final exams.

docs.title: 5. TARS Communication Protocol
docs.text:
Status: Shipped

  • The Hook: A phone inside your terminal.
  • Stack: Python, Socket Programming, Audio Encoding
  • Repo: THE-TARS-PROJECT/tars-comm

Most of my projects after 2024 are inspired by sci-fi movies. I was watching Tony Stark and Ivan Vonko talking on through that sci-fi ui interface. So, I decided to make one.

This is a terminal based voice-over-ip application that is like a phone (including phone book) but lives in your terminal

docs.title: 6. Bio-Silicon Synergetic Intelligent System
docs.text:
Status: Shipped

  • The Science: EEG Data Analysis for Neuro-research
  • Focus: Fault-tolerant Signal Processing
  • Repo: Raghav67816/Bio-Silicon...

After finishing 10th grade I randomly emailed an independent research group asking for some work, I started with making basic utility tools and they turned out to be really useful. So, I was assigned to build the core software of the project which involved reading and visualising complex EEG data.

In my opinion this is the best faul-tolerant system I have ever shipped.

There is a closed source version of this project which I can't share, but that one is more cool.

docs.title: 7. Eventium
docs.text:
Status: Shipped

  • Context: Built for Daydream Delhi
  • Stack: Full-stack Application
  • Repo: Raghav67816/eventium

I was the PoC Of Daydream Delhi and tbh the event very cool and bad at the same time. This is the only thing I wish I could do once again.

It was Day 2 dinner we ordered enough burgers but turned out most of the participants didn't get them, we checked the stock and it was perfect on the vendor side turns out participants secretly took multiple packs while volunteers were distributing it to others.

And I felt like Hack Club's Cockpit could have been better with a few modification. So, I made my own version of Cockpit with the tools which I believe would have helped the team a lot.

docs.title: Other Work
docs.text: I am constantly building and breaking things. You can find my full history of commits and experiments on my GitHub Profile.

docs.title: The Golden Downfall
docs.text:
TLDR;

What I was: Why I don't get result for the hard work I do ? Why always something bad happens with me ?

What I became: Results are not always materialistic. Sometimes a lesson is the fruit of hardwork

I participated in Hack Club's Juice and made a game inspired from Resident Evil 7 & Cry Of Fear.

Can't thank Thomas enough, even though I was not able to attend the event, it just changed me who I am completely. Basically, I qualified for the event, I had 400 USD in stipends to cover my flight.

I applied for passport and guess what HARASSMENT. To be very clear I am not afraid to say that Police took 6K+2K INR in bribe to get my verification cleared without delay. Yes, they were intentionally delaying it for money. They harassed my father till core. The ACP of the district are all di*kheads. I say it very clearly.

I went to Home Ministry of India for help, I explained them, I begged for help and he said "Going to different country is not a game there are rules" I just simply said WHAT RULES HUH ? THE RULE TO HARASS THE MIDDLE CLAS ? YOU OFFICERS TOOK BRIBE FROM ME TO PASS MY VERIFICATION, AND YOU TALKING ABOUT RULES they misbehaved and said TAKE YOUR FILES AND GO AWAY BEFORE I KICK YOU OUT

This was just unbelievable and I was furious. And since that day I hate the government. But you know, it wouldn't change anything, so I started to look for how to organise my own hackathons and after a few months I was selected as PoC Of Daydream Delhi and knew what my goal Open and Accessible Hackathon In India.

Me and my team tried our best and got IIT Delhi India's best engineering institute as venue, Scaler School Of Tech as sponsor (1K USD) along with StacksKB, India's best keyboard manufacturer.

There is a lot I can talk about Daydream Delhi but after everything I learned that It's not about how you do the work, but how you manage people

Participants of Daydream Delhi are now running their own local initiatives inspired by Daydream and I am invited as mentor and judge to one of the local competitions along with Joint Comissioner of the District so it was win for me.

We had participants who could not even afford travel and food. And they still attended and learned with Hack Club's and our sponsor's support.

There were a lot of times, when I got into dilemmas and yes I took the right decisions.There exist people who can't hear a no or just think everybody except them is fool.

And thanks to Daydream team specially Renran and Deven for being empathetic with me.

I am now looking to organise more events because I know it will be different this time

PS: The ACP to whom I handed 2K INR as bribe, came to my school as a chief guest in school assembly to lecture about honesty and hardwork. Can you believe this ?

docs.title: The New Life
docs.text:
TLDR;

What I was: An arrogant popular kid with good amount and quality of technical skills.

What I became (2023): I am not the main character, I am just another living being with some good skills.

I had good technical skills as compared to my peers. So, I was kind of famous during my school life. But back then when I was in class 9, I was something different a hot-headed guy with an attitude that he is the only best person in the room.

So, 9th standard started and I was given a team to lead for AI School Exhibition project. We worked and completed the project. The problem was my team didn't knew much of the technical details of the project.

Now comes the exhibition day. I was out for another inter-school compeition. And boom it failed in front of the guests my team was embarassed.

Next day, I was scolded of my attitude. And I was like Who are they to point fingers at my project, it's just that Blynk's new system is sh*t and they can't handle it

As a result I spent a few weeks designing and building an automation platform easy enough to be used by a layman.

SIMPLE & FLEXIBLE

Project worked superb Atomberg Inc loved it and me and my friend were invited to IIT Bombay's Techfest 2022 Asia's biggest technical fest. And guess what we won Youngest National Finalists & Budding Innovators award. And we were the youngest participants ever.

This is from where my fav PFP came from.

After that, came 2023 10th standard. I thought like oh let's do this, I am sure I will win this, with this attitude I aimed for Samsung Solve For Tomorrow and dreamt of winning it. But guess what I didn't even pass 1st round

It took me a week but I understood, life is not something I can get much control of. It's just that I have to go with the flow. Not life which has to go with my flow.

And I met really great people like Khuzeyhan Ozdemir, from George Mason University now Director at NobleReach Foundation.
